name: Lohagad Fort
tagline: The easiest classic Sahyadri fort trek — views over Pawna Lake in under an hour
seoTitle: Lohagad Fort Solo Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Solo trekker's guide to Lohagad Fort near Lonavala — the easiest classic Sahyadri trek, ASI rules, season, and packing.

seasons.label: Jun – Sep
seasons.sub: Monsoon — the classic season, but very crowded weekends

seasons.label: Oct – Feb
seasons.sub: Quieter, clear views over Pawna Lake

routeOptions.name: From Lohagadwadi
routeOptions.notes: Well-worn path, doable in sandals by fit trekkers, but proper shoes recommended in monsoon.

permits.name: ASI site rules
permits.fullName: Archaeological Survey of India — protected monument
permits.where: N/A — no entry fee, but rules apply on site
permits.notes: No cooking/open fires allowed on the fort.

safety.intro: Lohagad is about as low-risk as Sahyadri treks get — the main hazards are crowding and slippery stone on monsoon weekends.

cards.title: Before you go
items: Go early on monsoon weekends — this is one of the most crowded treks near Mumbai/Pune
Carry cash for parking/local food stalls at the base

cards.title: On the trail
items: The connecting ridge (naagin) to twin fort Visapur is narrow and exposed — take care in wind/rain
No cooking fires allowed on the fort (ASI rule) — carry ready-to-eat food

cards.title: Solo-specific
items: Very beginner and solo-friendly — always crowded enough to not feel isolated
Still keep footing careful on the exposed ridge sections regardless of crowd

items.name: Grippy shoes for the monsoon steps
Ready-to-eat snacks (no fires allowed on fort)

gettingThere.intro: Probably the easiest trek on this whole list to reach — a train to Malavli and a short rickshaw ride.

steps.title: Train to Malavli or Lonavala
steps.body: Frequent local trains from Mumbai and Pune reach Malavli station (closest to Lohagad and Visapur) or Lonavala — roughly 2 hrs from Mumbai, 1 hr from Pune.

steps.title: Malavli to Bhaje village
steps.body: From Malavli station, a shared auto or rickshaw covers the ~4–5 km to Bhaje village, roughly 15–20 min. More frequent at weekends; on weekdays you may need to negotiate a dedicated rickshaw.

steps.title: Trek
steps.body: An easy, popular 1–1.5 hr climb from Bhaje along a well-defined path and the famous 'Vinchu Kata' (scorpion's tail) approach.

gettingThere.permitNote: No entry fee. This is one of the most accessible and well-marked treks in the Sahyadris — a good first solo outing. Note the ASI rule against cooking or open fires on the fort.

onTrail.note: Not customary — the trail is well-marked and busy

onTrail.item: Food and tea at Bhaje or on the fort
